data_source.name: Nevada Department of Taxation: Cannabis Tax Revenue reports (FY25, FY26, FY27)
data_source.notes: Taxable sales reported by cannabis dispensaries and consumption lounges, by month of the Department's accounting period. Per the Department, the figure includes adult-use and medical cannabis plus other tangible property sold by licensees, so adult_use and medical are null and only total is given. The October 2024 accounting period closed early, shifting some revenue into later months. Annual figures are fiscal years (July-June); FY2024 and FY2025 totals are from the CCB/Taxation joint release of Feb 5, 2026.

monthly.note: Department of Taxation footnote: the October 2024 accounting period closed early, so part of October revenue was recorded in later months

annual.basis: Department of Taxation FY26 cannabis revenue report (fiscal-year-to-date column)

tax_note: Adult-use sales carry a 10% state retail cannabis excise tax, and a 15% wholesale excise tax applies to both adult-use and medical cannabis, on top of sales tax (Nevada Department of Taxation).
summary: Nevada's market leans heavily on Las Vegas tourism, with Clark County accounting for about three-quarters of taxable sales. Dispensaries and consumption lounges reported $51.5 million in taxable sales for August 2026. Annual taxable sales have fallen three years running, from $829.2 million in fiscal 2024 to $757.7 million in fiscal 2025 and $696.0 million in fiscal 2026. Lower prices, softer tourist spending and competition from California and Arizona all weigh on revenue. Consumption lounges add a small amount of on-site sales.

faq.q: How much cannabis does Nevada sell a month?
faq.a: Nevada licensees reported $51.5 million in taxable cannabis sales for August 2026, according to the Department of Taxation.

faq.q: How much cannabis did Nevada sell last fiscal year?
faq.a: Taxable sales were $696.0 million in fiscal 2026 (July 2025 to June 2026), down from $757.7 million in fiscal 2025.

faq.q: Does Nevada split adult-use and medical sales?
faq.a: Not in its monthly sales data. The Department of Taxation reports one taxable sales figure covering adult-use, medical and other items sold by licensees.
